hook: 400,000 gallons hit this launch pad in one test.
narration: Four hundred thousand gallons of water rush onto this launch pad when the Moon rocket lifts off.
This was the test, at Kennedy Space Center on October twenty-fourth, 2023.
The water pours across the deck and off every side of the mobile launcher, the steel tower that holds the rocket.
At ignition, a rocket makes a pressure wave and a roar strong enough to damage the rocket, the capsule and the pad. The water soaks up both.
It was the third test in a series to prove the system was ready for Artemis II.
outcome: The pad drained dry, and in April 2026 Artemis II lifted off from this same pad.

location_card.place: Launch Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida

title: 400,000 gallons flood a launch pad
description:
On Oct. 24, 2023, NASA ran a water flow test of the sound suppression and overpressure protection system on the mobile launcher at Launch Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center, ahead of Artemis II.
